pr_title: kvserver: fail helpfully in and deflake TestOptimisticEvalNoContention
pr_body:
We've seen[^1] that in rare cases, the limited scan in that test does
not successfully evaluate optimistically, and ends up blocking on an
intent indefinitely.

This commit adds a timeout to the scan as well as wraps it in a verbose
trace so that we can understand this problem better the next time we
see it.

I looked at the optimistic read path and see no obvious way this can
be turned off (short of randomizing the cluster setting[^2], which we
don't seem to be doing). So perhaps the read hits a retry or the like,
but either way it will be less poking around in the dark once we get
a repro after this commit.

[^1]: https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/issues/123986#issuecomment-2107606634
[^2]: https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/issues/123986#issuecomment-2107606634

Closes #130973.

Epic: none
Release note: None

I'll try to repro for a little longer before I seriously believe that this is what's happening.

Okay I think I've got it. Reminder, we're seeing the following:

- `Put(a)Put(b)Commit` is run as a 1PC txn (in my current version of the failing test; it's not 1PC in the original test but it shouldn't mattern).
- when this returns, we run `db.Get(a)`, `db.Get(b)`.
- when this returns, we run `Scan(a,c,limit=1)` and this first takes the optimistic path, but then checks latches and **finds the latch for `Put(a)Put(b)Commit` still in place**.
- this fails the test (simplified but true).

The highlighted bit is what we need to understand. Here's how this can happen:

- `Put(a)Put(b)Commit` runs (1PC). Because we're acking writes before they apply (pipelined writes), this returns while the write is still inflight. I don't think this is necessary, but it probably helps actually hitting the right interleaving (when I turn it off, I can't repro).
- our `db.Get(a)` can race with the 1PC txn finishining application. Concretely, the 1PC can be in the middle of its call to `ec.repl.concMgr.FinishReq`[^1].
- concretely, in the middle of `(*spanlatch.Manager).Release`[^2].
- more concretely, it may already have called `lg.done.signal()`, but not yet `m.remove(ctx, lg)`.
- because `lg.done` has been signaled, `db.Get(a)` and `db.Get(b)` can go through and read the correct write.
- `Scan(a,c,limit=1)` arrives and optimistically evaluates. Then it checks latches - they are still there.
- at some point - in fact momentarily - `m.remove(ctx, lg)` will be called, but it is too late.
- the scan flunked out of the optimistic path.

If I replace the order of `m.remove` and `lg.done.signal`, this problem cannot occur. The test is stable. If I don't reorder but put in a well-timed sleep, the test fails deterministically:

```go
func (m *Manager) Release(ctx context.Context, lg *Guard) {
	lg.done.signal()
	if lg.snap != nil {
		lg.snap.close()
	}
	if ctx.Value(5) != nil {
		time.Sleep(100 * time.Millisecond)
	}
	m.remove(ctx, lg)
```

@nvanbenschoten are we okay reordering these or is this a performance optimization that we want to keep? Something else we could do to address this is to never bail on latches that have already been signaled. Concretely, in `CheckOptimisticNoConflicts`[^1] we'd modify the `overlaps` method to ignore latches that have `it.Cur().g.done.signaled()`.

[^2]: https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/51de177f88011d8e29e103973c1a8d17aa1dc947/pkg/kv/kvserver/spanlatch/manager.go#L641-L661
[^1]: https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/51de177f88011d8e29e103973c1a8d17aa1dc947/pkg/kv/kvserver/replica_send.go#L1360

> @nvanbenschoten are we okay reordering these or is this a performance optimization that we want to keep?

I think it would be unfortunate to reorder these and incur the performance penalty just for test cases like these. Concretely, this would delay requests that are waiting on latches, even when they could have already started running.

> Something else we could do to address this is to never bail on latches that have already been signaled. Concretely, in CheckOptimisticNoConflicts we'd modify the overlaps method to ignore latches that have it.Cur().g.done.signaled().

I don't think this would be correct. CheckOptimisticNoConflicts checks whether there were any conflicting requests at any time during the optimistic evaluation, not just whether any conflicts are still running at the time of the check. So there could have been conflicting requests which did evaluate concurrently, but then completed and signalled during optimistic evaluation of another request. We would need to find a way to distinguish those from conflicting requests which were already signalled at the time that the optimistic evaluating request snapshotted the latch manager.

My suggestion would be to remove the `Get`s in these tests (`setupDBAndWriteAAndB`, `BenchmarkOptimisticEvalForLocks`, `BenchmarkOptimisticEval`) and to run with 1PC + `DisableCanAckBeforeReplication` instead. The `Get`s are already a "hack" to wait for completion of the async portions of these writes during setup. Might as well just remove the async work.

> I don't think this would be correct.

Good catch.

> I think it would be unfortunate to reorder these and incur the performance penalty just for test cases like these. Concretely, this would delay requests that are waiting on latches, even when they could have already started running.
> My suggestion would be to remove the Gets in these tests (setupDBAndWriteAAndB, BenchmarkOptimisticEvalForLocks, BenchmarkOptimisticEval) and to run with 1PC + DisableCanAckBeforeReplication instead. The Gets are already a "hack" to wait for completion of the async portions of these writes during setup. Might as well just remove the async work.

Ack, done - see the second commit (first is unchanged I think).

> Do we need DisablePipelining if we're going to CommitInBatch?

We shouldn't, removed.

TFTR!
